OMIM:612164.summary_plain: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 4 is strongly linked to STXBP1. The graph also suggests STXBP1 variants may reduce MUNC18-1/STXBP1 function and synaptic vesicle release. Separate registry studies focus on STXBP1-related disorders, which may help with natural history and trial readiness.

steps.text: The core link is clear: STXBP1 causes Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 4. This is a supported disease-gene relationship, not just a guess. [E00001]

Several human reports suggest that STXBP1 pathogenic variants may lead to loss of STXBP1/MUNC18-1 function and reduced synaptic vesicle release. That is a plausible mechanism, but it is still a gene-function link rather than proof of one shared pathway in every patient. [M5149905a, M09610d0b, Ma389ab1a]

There are STXBP1-related studies in the graph that may be useful for family-facing research or natural-history planning. These include a European study on clinical trial readiness, a natural history study, and a registry on epilepsy-dyskinesia syndromes. [T00064, T00068, T00069, T00070]

The graph also shows phenotype similarity to other epileptic encephalopathy conditions. These are hypothesis-generating only, not evidence that the diseases share the same cause or the same treatment response. [E00226, E00225, E00222]

uncertainties: The graph does not say which STXBP1 variant types are most relevant for this patient group, so variant-specific effects are not established here. [M5149905a, M09610d0b, Ma389ab1a]

The registry entries are named in the graph, but the scope and eligibility details are not fully shown here, so it is unclear whether a specific family would fit each study. [T00064, T00068, T00069, T00070]
The phenotype-similarity edges are computed hypotheses, so they should not be used as evidence of a shared mechanism or a treatment match. [E00226, E00225, E00222]
